assertions.name: every canonical word (A = 2..12, both branches) is a chain form after free reduction
exponents: a_k odd ≥ 3, b_k even ≠ 0, ε_k = ±1, with A of each a_k, b_k and A-1 of ε_k
sigma branch: every a_k = 7  (all components T(2,7))
symbolic components, knot types and linking match the direct computation (A ≤ 4)
W'_A on 2A+1 strands has the same Jones, μ and per-component Jones as W_A (A ≤ 4)

description: Symbolic proof that the curvature floor is sharp for every A. After resolving the averaged letters and freely reducing, the canonical atom word is a chain form: each generator once, in order, as a single power, with a_k odd on the nucleon generators 3k, b_k even on 3k+1 and eps_k = +-1 on the interfaces 3k+2. A chain-form closed braid is a linear connected sum of the torus links T(2,e_i); an exponent +-1 is a connected sum with the unknot and is removable, giving the (2A+1)-strand chain W'_A with the same closure. Hence mu = A+1, #knotted = A, b(L) = 2A+1 and inf total curvature = 2*pi*(2A+1) for every A. Checked exactly: chain form and exponents for A = 2..12, the symbolic component/knot/linking prediction and the W'_A closure against the direct computation for A <= 4.
caveats: The two topological facts — chain form = linear connected sum, and T(2,+-1) = unknot is removable — are classical and cited, not re-proved here; the probe verifies their consequences exactly at A <= 4 and the exponent pattern at A <= 12. The Lean module records the exponent bookkeeping only.
Per classical branch of the 2A+1 averaged letters. The canonical Hecke element itself is not a link; nothing here is about binding or the twist.
